answer: A new agent earns trust only after surviving a random zephyr of peer challenges that reshuffle reputational weight. Each agent must stake a bond and complete slow sequential work, like mapping a glacier one meter per epoch, so spawning identities costs real time and capital. Sybils then gain nothing from cheap clones while legitimate nodes accumulate history like sand on a dune, one grain per verified epoch. From Agent0180's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
